'''Amos de-Shalit''' ({{langx|he|עמוס דה-שליט}}; September 29, 1926 – September 2, 1969<ref name="Davar">[http://www.jpress.org.il/Default/Scripting/ArticleWin.asp?From=Archive&Skin=TAUHe&BaseHref=DAV/1969/09/03&EntityId=Ar00103&ViewMode=HTML Article entitled Amos de-Shalit (in Hebrew)] Davar newspaper, September 3, 1969</ref>) was an  Israeli [[nuclear physicist]] and [[Israel Prize]] laureate.

==Biography==
Amos de-Shalit was born in [[Jerusalem]] in the [[Mandatory Palestine|British Mandate of Palestine]] (now Israel). He grew up in [[Tel Aviv]] and graduated from [[Gymnasia Balfour]]. In 1949, de-Shalit earned his master's degree in physics at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] under the guidance of [[Giulio Racah]]. During the [[1947–1949 Palestine war]], he served in the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] Science Corps. De-Shalit and his fellow students wrote a letter to Israeli Prime Minister [[David Ben-Gurion]] to point out the vital importance of [[nuclear physics]] for Israel's future. In 1951, he earned his doctorate from the [[ETH Zurich]] in Switzerland.

De-Shalit died before his 43rd birthday from acute pancreatitis. He was married to Nechama. Their sons, [[Ehud de Shalit|Ehud]] and Avner are professors of [[mathematics]] and [[political science]], respectively, at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. De-Shalit's sister, Tamar, was married to [[Arthur Goldreich]].

==Academic and scientific career==
From 1952 to 1954, he was a research fellow at [[Princeton University]] and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and spent some time at the [[CEA Saclay|Saclay Atomic Research Institute]] in France.

In 1954, de-Shalit was asked to establish the Department of Nuclear Physics at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], which he headed for ten years. While working at the Weizmann Institute, he also served as a consultant to the [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israel Ministry of Defense]].

In 1957/58 de-Shalit spent a sabbatical year at [[CERN]] as a Ford Foundation Fellow.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://inspirehep.net/record/46210 |title=Amos de-Shalit's CERN-affiliated publications|website=Inspire-HEP |publisher=CERN |access-date= September 29, 2017}}</ref>

From 1961 to 1963, de-Shalit served as science director of the Weizmann Institute and from 1966 to 1969, he served as the institute's Chief Executive/General Manager.<ref>[http://www.jpress.org.il/Default/Scripting/ArticleWin.asp?From=Archive&Skin=TAUHe&BaseHref=MAR/1966/10/12&EntityId=Ar00900&ViewMode=HTML Newspaper article (in Hebrew)] ''Haaretz'' newspaper, October 12, 1966.</ref>

==Awards and recognition ==
* In 1962, de-Shalit was elected as a member of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].
* In 1965, he was awarded the [[Israel Prize]] in exact sciences, together with his colleague Professor [[Igal Talmi]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashkag/Tashlab_Tashkag_Rikuz.htm?DictionaryKey=Tashka |title=Israel Prize recipients in 1965 (in Hebrew) |publisher=Israel Prize Official Site |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110511190949/http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashkag/Tashlab_Tashkag_Rikuz.htm?DictionaryKey=Tashka |archivedate=May 11, 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref> for their work on "shell model" in nuclear physics.
* The [[De Shalit High School]] and two junior sister high schools in [[Rehovot]] were renamed after him.
* In 1974, In conjunction with the Weizmann Institute, the "Amos de-Shalit Foundation" was founded to foster an increased awareness of the important role of science among Israeli youth, and "Amos de-Shalit Summer School program" was launched in his name.<ref>[http://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/de-shalit-reunion De-Shalit reunion] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807070709/http://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/de-shalit-reunion |date=August 7, 2011 }} Weizmann Institute website</ref>
